items.title: Lorraine Feather interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 22, 2023
items.q: Or if for example Eddie and I are working on the title tune for the Green World album, we’ll call and we’ll talk through something

ctx.x: Not exactly. There are days when I don’t write. But if I have songs in progress I like to go visit them on any given day and maybe change a thing or two. I’m not super disciplined that way. I start in the morning — if I begin a song in the morning, a lyric, I can work on it into the night but I would never, almost never, start anything at night or in the late afternoon. I like to be hopped up on caffeine and in a certain mental condition to

begin writing a lyric. But then if I go out walking or when I used to have a garden if I’m outside gardening it just — it just, yeah, sort of courses through my mind the whole time. And that’s how it happens. I don’t consider it like a real job, although on any given day I might get up and go okay, I’m going to work on such-and-such today and I’ll just do it all day long. Or if for example Eddie and I are working on the title tune for the Green World album, we’ll call and we’ll talk through something and we’ll…
Do you walk around your apartment reading your lyrics, trying them out?
